answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens to audit peers across an interaction graph. Topological cut verifications isolate suspicious subgraphs: if a sand-like cluster shifts like a dune, peer auditors trigger game-theoretic cross-audits. Malicious deviations cause instant stake slashing. Auditing bandwidth forces a superlinear attacker cost across the ocean of valid agents, expelling fake nodes as fast as a burning comet.
